edges.description: The initial bite wound heals, then reactivates into an indurated or ulcerated lesion as the S. minus form declares itself.
S. minus can spread beyond the bite exposure to produce systemic rat-bite fever.
Reactivation produces an indurated or ulcerated bite-site lesion.
The reactivated lesion spreads to regional lymphatics.
S. minus infection produces the febrile syndrome of sodoku.
The febrile illness may relapse in the spirillary form.
Systemic rat-bite fever inflammation can produce a rash, though rash is rare in the spirillary form.
